claim: By default, Capacity Reservations automatically match new and running instances with matching attributes (instance type, platform, Availability Zone and tenancy); you can instead target a reservation so only chosen instances run in it.

evidence.quote: Capacity Reservations can only be used by instances that match their attributes. By default, Capacity Reservations automatically match new instances and running instances that have matching attributes (instance type, platform, Availability Zone, and tenancy). This means that any instance with matching attributes automatically runs in the Capacity Reservation. However, you can also target a Capacity Reservation for specific workloads.

claim: Capacity Reservations are charged at the equivalent On-Demand rate whether or not you run instances in the reserved capacity; when a matching instance runs, you pay only for the instance and nothing for the reservation, with no upfront or additional charges.

evidence.quote: Capacity Reservations are charged at the equivalent On-Demand rate whether you run instances in reserved capacity or not, including any applicable regional surcharge for Dedicated Instances. If you do not use the reservation, this shows up as unused reservation on your Amazon EC2 bill. When you run an instance that matches the attributes of a reservation, you just pay for the instance and nothing for the reservation. There are no upfront or additional charges.

evidence.quote: Dedicated Instances are EC2 instances that run on hardware that's dedicated to a single AWS account. This means that Dedicated Instances are physically isolated at the host hardware level from instances that belong to other AWS accounts, even if those accounts are linked to a single payer account. However, Dedicated Instances might share hardware with other instances from the same AWS account that are not Dedicated Instances.

If you stop and start a Dedicated Instance, it might not run on the same host. Similarly, you cannot target a specific host on which to launch or run an instance. Additionally, Dedicated Instances provide limited support for Bring Your Own License (BYOL).

claim: An Amazon EC2 Dedicated Host is a physical server fully dedicated for your use; it gives visibility and control over instance placement and supports host affinity, and you can optionally share its instance capacity with other AWS accounts.
question: What is a Dedicated Host?

values.spoken: you control where instances are placed

values.display: optionally choose to share the instance capacity

evidence.quote: An Amazon EC2 Dedicated Host is a physical server that is fully dedicated for your use. You can optionally choose to share the instance capacity with other AWS accounts.

Dedicated Hosts provide visibility and control over instance placement and they support host affinity. This means that you can launch and run instances on specific hosts, and you can ensure that instances run only on specific hosts.

claim: Auto-placement is set at the host level; when it is disabled (the default for new Dedicated Hosts) the host accepts only host-tenancy launches that name its host ID, and when it is enabled the host accepts any untargeted host-tenancy launch that matches its instance type configuration.

values.spoken: auto-placement is off by default

values.display: that specify its unique host ID
values.spoken: when off, only launches that name the host ID land there

values.display: accepts any untargeted, host tenancy instance launches

evidence.quote: When auto-placement is **disabled** for a Dedicated Host, it accepts only host tenancy instance launches that specify its unique host ID. This is the default setting for new Dedicated Hosts.
When auto-placement is **enabled** for a Dedicated Host, it accepts any untargeted, host tenancy instance launches that match its instance type configuration.

claim: Host affinity is set at the instance level; with affinity set to Host, an instance launched onto a specific host always restarts on the same host if stopped, and with Default it can restart on any available host while trying the last host on a best-effort basis.
question: What does Dedicated Host affinity do when an instance is stopped and started?

values.display: always restarts on the same host if stopped
values.spoken: with Host affinity the instance comes back to the same host

values.display: it can be restarted on any available host
values.spoken: with Default affinity it can move

evidence.quote: When affinity is set to `Host`, an instance launched onto a specific host always restarts on the same host if stopped. This applies to both targeted and untargeted launches.

When affinity is set to `Default`, and you stop and restart the instance, it can be restarted on any available host. However, it tries to launch back onto the last Dedicated Host on which it ran (on a best-effort basis).

qualifiers.scope: EC2 Fleet and Spot Fleet Capacity Rebalancing

evidence.quote: When a Spot Instance is at an elevated risk of interruption, Amazon EC2 sends a [rebalance recommendation](rebalance-recommendations.md). If Capacity Rebalancing is enabled, the rebalance recommendation triggers the launch of a new Spot Instance before the at-risk instance is interrupted.
Capacity Rebalancing is available only for fleets of type `maintain`.
